m1_reencoding.formula: x = stored raw value read as float64; c = min(max(x, clip_lo), clip_hi); z = (c - new_mean) / new_std if governing_mask == 1 else 0.0; cast to float32
m1_reencoding.fit_population: FULL TRAIN: all 64 user buckets, split = TRAIN, rows with the governing mask = 1 (M1FIT:2-68,73)
m1_reencoding.fit_grain: executed v1 convention: one unweighted row per TRAIN row of model_ready features.parquet, i.e. one per canonical representative = one per TRAIN decision (DATA_CONTRACT.md:227-234), regardless of loss_mask or target availability; values clipped at the RECORDED bounds (M1FIT:74); population standard deviation (ddof = 0) as in EDA/pipeline6.py:427-433. M1FIT reproduces the recorded all-row normalizer with the same grain (M1FIT:90-94,102,118-122,130), so only the row filter changes
m1_reencoding.source_of_numbers: M1FIT valid_mean / valid_std; train_valid block repeats them (M1FIT:85-89,113-117)
m1_reencoding.not_used_for_fit: vs_valid_drift_only blocks (M1FIT:95-99,123-127) are reported drift only
m1_reencoding.rezero: mandatory: without it the new encoding of an unavailable row would be -1.6924 (user) and -7.1271 (session), far outside the valid range
m1_reencoding.clip_bound_disclosure: clip bounds are the recorded all-row quantiles (clip_lo 0.0 is pinned by the masked zeros, EDA/pipeline6.py:395-398); they are kept by decision and valid-only clip rates are NOT established

T08.package_text: missing/invalid-price masks, finite values, zero variance and all-missing features
cases: price NULL, negative, NaN, +inf, 0 and a conflicting block: log1p_price encodes 0.0, flags as specified
every V2 tensor value finite on synthetic and on one real bucket per split
zero-variance column (std <= 1e-12 or hi <= lo) is constant -> 0.0
all-missing column (no valid TRAIN row) is constant -> 0.0
degenerate M1 valid std is refused
negative_controls: inject NaN into a raw column -> must raise
a std = 0 column not marked constant -> must raise, not divide
price_missing = 1 with a non-zero stored log1p_price -> output still 0.0
T08.proves: the missing/finite/constant rules of the transform
T08.does_not_prove: that future data has no new invalid-price mode

T09.package_text: valid-only scaler fitting excludes structural zeros/padding; unknowns re-zero after transform
cases: synthetic fit from mask = 1 rows only reproduces the fixture mean/std; PAD rows never enter a fit
real data: the two M1 valid mean/std recomputed on full TRAIN at the stated grain match M1FIT within 1e-9 relative (DONE: PPSI/g0/receipts_qa02/OI04_M1_REPRODUCTION.json, abs diff 0.0)
real data: the F-1 valid-only fit equals mean 0.002065693626402541, std 0.9945344391661521, n_valid 48,434,230 (PPSI/g0/receipts_qa02/OI03_F1_PRICE_REZERO.json:23-32)
every rezero_map_v2 entry yields exactly 0.0 when its condition holds and (clip(x)-mean)/std otherwise
the cold-user V2 vector equals cold_user_vector_v2_expected on real has_history = 0 rows
F-1: recent_price_supported = 1 with current price_missing or price_conflict gives 0.0
negative_controls: a fit that includes mask = 0 rows must reproduce the OLD all-row normalizer (M1FIT normalizer_reproduced_by_all_rows = true) and be rejected
removing an M1 entry from the re-zero map must surface z = -1.6924 / -7.1271 and fail

F-1: a current_minus_recent_mean_log_price fit that includes the 117,315 current-price-unknown raw zeros must reproduce the old std 0.9933321718650419 (and mean 0.0020607022950704136) and be rejected (G0B:16)
T09.does_not_prove: any ranking effect of the M1 repair

T10.package_text: scalers/vocabularies fit on TRAIN; deliberate future-only category rejected as known
cases: every fitted statistic in TRANSFORM_STATE is traced to split = TRAIN rows only
a category, brand, main category and product first seen after TRAIN maps to OOV = 2, never to a known index
a product outside the support>=5 catalogue maps to OOV = 2 in context and is not a class
negative_controls: a fit on TRAIN plus VALIDATION_SELECT must give a different mean (M1FIT vs_valid_drift_only blocks show the drift) and be rejected
a vocabulary built with a future-only value must be detected
T10.proves: TRAIN-only fitting of every shared object
T10.does_not_prove: absence of pooled bootstrap information (it is present by design and disclosed)

T11.package_text: no double-log/standardize; explicit raw/logged/normalized state contract
cases: every V2 column carries a declared state; the transform is a state machine RAW/LOG1P -> CLIP -> ZSCORE -> REZERO with illegal transitions raising
stored log1p_* columns are never logged again
valid negative z values (e.g. current_minus_recent_mean_log_price) are accepted
cyclic, binary, share, flag and mask columns pass through unchanged
negative_controls: applying log1p twice to a log1p fixture must raise or fail the value check
standardizing an already z-scored batch must be detected
T11.proves: each column's transform chain matches its declared state
T11.does_not_prove: that the declared state is the best encoding

T12.package_text: reconstructable duplicate algebra + full population contradictions and negative controls; future-relevant dead flags retained
cases: synthetic fixtures for every DROP_REDUNDANT synthetic_cases list
RC1..RC7 run on every batch before any column is dropped

full-population counts: DUP for TRAIN and VALIDATION_SELECT; RC1..RC6 on merged VALIDATION incl. the 3,427,555 VC rows all 0 and the six dead flags 0 non-zero on VC (DONE: PPSI/g0/receipts_qa02/OI06_RC_VALIDATION.json:10-122)
the six DEAD_IN_TRAIN flags, price_zero and main_category_missing are present at their v1 indices
negative_controls: perturb one row per identity (item count +2, rotation by 2*pi*2/24, one flipped mask bit, elapsed +1e-3) and the check must fail
a schema variant that drops a dead flag must be rejected by the schema validator
T12.proves: the removed columns are recoverable from kept inputs on the checked populations and the dead flags stay available
T12.does_not_prove: equal trained accuracy, or anything about TEST before it is loaded

T14.package_text: local feature provenance, as-of item-observed-age, no cross-client user-history contamination
cases: each kept channel carries its locality label; the schema validator rejects a channel without one
two-user interleaved replay: user A's LOCAL_HISTORY values are unchanged when user B's events are added or removed (EDA/userctx.py:156-236 against the slow reference :243-309)
item age: an item first seen after TRAIN gives item_age_unavailable = 1 and 0.0; an item whose first TRAIN sighting equals block_ts is unavailable (EDA/pipeline6.py:151-152,181)
SHARED_TRAIN_STATISTIC objects have identical sha256 in every method's run manifest
negative_controls: an unsorted stream that interleaves two users must be detected
a first-seen computed over all months must change item age on a fixture and be rejected
T14.proves: provenance labels, as-of item age and per-user isolation of history features
